- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts show gradual, linear upward drift with no sharp peaks, while true outcomes often spike upward early (e.g., 75–80 range) then drop.
- Model fails to capture early spikes; true values often exceed forecast by 2–5 points in first 5–7 days.
- After spikes, model continues upward trend while true values often show mean reversion or sharp downward correction.
- Model overestimates late-period values (last 5–7 days) — true values are typically 1–3 points lower.
- Model lacks sensitivity to recent high volatility; fails to adjust downward after sharp spikes.
- Forecast assumes smooth trend; true outcomes show more volatility and non-linear corrections.
- Model tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in downward corrections.
- Model overcorrects after spikes — forecasts overshoot true values by 1–3 points in mid-period.
- Model underestimates mean reversion — fails to anticipate sharp drops after peaks.
